Hi Julia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Summary of customer goals (from call):
- Validate model quality on clinical note summarization and patient triage flows
- Ensure 95th-percentile latency under 350ms for single-turn summary requests
- Confirm cost and throughput for production-like traffic patterns

Proposed POC scope / success criteria:
- Run a 2-week POC using your redacted sample dataset (10k notes) and our recommended model (open-llm-v2 quantized)
- Success = 95% of summaries meet your QA checklist (sample-based review) AND 95th-percentile latency < 350ms under agreed workload profile
- Error rate (API errors or model failures) < 0.5%

Workload intake we need from you (please fill the attached spreadsheet):
- Typical RPS (average) and peak RPS (1-minute sustained peak)
- Average and 95th-percentile input token length (per request) and expected output token lengths
- Concurrent connections (number of concurrent clients) and burst patterns (how often do you see 15+ RPS bursts)
- Auth/traffic routing notes (region constraints, egress rules)

Timeline and ownership:
- Kickoff call week of 2027-06-07 (owner: Ben Carter)
- Workload ingestion & test harness setup: 3 business days after kickoff (owner: Marissa Cole)
- Initial baseline run & first QA pass: end of week 1 (owner: Marissa / AcmeHealth review)
- Iteration and tuning week 2; final report and recommendation at end of week 2 (owner: Ben)

Next steps (what I will do):
1) Attach the workload intake spreadsheet + sample POC timeline (attached).
2) Schedule kickoff — propose Tue 2027-06-08 10:00am PT.
3) Marissa will follow up with test harness details and requirements.

Can you/ACME complete the workload spreadsheet and confirm kickoff time?

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,

Thanks Ben — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side to help you size the PoC: 

Workload profile (prod-ish):
- Typical average RPS: 6 RPS during business hours (EST)
- Sustained peak: 25 RPS for up to 10 minutes during reports generation
- Sporadic bursts: 100 RPS for ~60s (rare, 1-2x/day) during batch ingestion windows
- Concurrency: ~40 concurrent clients (mobile + backend), most requests are single-turn summaries

Token profile (approx):
- Average input: 450 tokens
- 95th percentile input: 1,800 tokens (longest notes)
- Average output: 120 tokens
- 95th output: 350 tokens

Success criteria comments:  
- The QA checklist will be provided by our clinical ops team — we'll evaluate a random sample of 500 summaries for accuracy and hallucination rate.
- Latency: P95 under 350ms is our target, but we can tolerate 400ms for the longest (1,800-token) inputs if quality is improved.

Security/compliance note:
- We'll only send de-identified notes for the trial. Our infra team (it@acmehealth.com) will need a short diagram of network egress and any proxy endpoints.

I'll fill and return the intake spreadsheet by EOD Friday 2027-06-11. Kickoff on Tue 2027-06-08 10:00am PT works for me.

— Julia
Director, Clinical AI | AcmeHealth
Julia.Chen@acmehealth.com

Thanks Julia — great detail, that's exactly what we needed. A few notes and confirmations: 

- We can support your burst profile with our autoscaling + warm pool; Marissa will size the initial instance pool to handle 100 RPS bursts with target P95 latency goals.
- For the longest inputs (1,800 tokens) we'll likely recommend a slightly higher CPU/GPU profile to keep inference latency acceptable — Marissa will include two profile options in the kickoff runbook.
- We'll add an ingestion test to simulate the 60s 100 RPS burst and measure degradation/fallover.

Next steps (confirmed):
1) Julia to return completed intake spreadsheet by 2027-06-11.
